reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services is the cloud computing arm of Amazon, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and its parent company is publicly traded under the ticker AMZN. The company's SageMaker site describes the next generation of Amazon SageMaker as a center for data, analytics, and AI, built around SageMaker Unified Studio, which the company says brings together AWS machine learning and analytics capabilities with unified access to data. The site lists SageMaker AI tools including HyperPod, JumpStart, and MLOps, along with Amazon Q Developer, which it describes as a generative AI assistant for software development. It also references Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon SageMaker Catalog.

Two AI products are tracked for the company. Amazon SageMaker is listed as a cloud AI service covering full machine learning lifecycle management, model monitoring, bias detection, and explainability tools. AWS Bedrock is listed as a managed foundation model API service with IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and AgentCore for agent orchestration. The site's customer quotes include an automotive company describing use of SageMaker to unify and govern data across connected car, sales, manufacturing, and supply chain units, and Carrier describing use of SageMaker Unified Studio for data discovery, processing, and model development.

Among the facts held, Amazon Web Services is named in a case in the District Court, D. Delaware, Haugland v. Anthropic PBC. The company's SEC filings show a CIK of 0001018724, a last revenue form of 10-K for the period ending 2025-12-31, and last revenue of 716924000000 USD.
